newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury issues new securities reporting rule.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury issues new securities reporting rule.

text.p: The Treasury Department issued a new rule on Wednesday requiring anyone who owns $2 billion or more of a specific government security to report it to the Treasury if asked to do so.
The long-awaited rule is in response to "squeezes" that occurred in 1991 when some buyers were able to acquire huge holdings in certain Treasury securities and so manipulate prices for them.

The rule is intended "to provide the Treasury and other securities regulators with information on concentrations of control that will enable them to understand better the possible reasons for apparent significant price distortions and the causes of market shortages in certain Treasury securities," a written summary said.

Treasury emphasized that it anticipated making such reporting requests infrequently and that it saw no inherent harm or manipulative intent in an investor acquiring such a large holding of a government security.
Any person or entity, including a private foreign securities company or a domestic one, that has $2 billion or more of a U.S. government security must keep records.

Reports on the holdings must be supplied to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York within 3-1/2 days if Treasury requests them. Not many market participants have such large holdings of any one security.

"We're talking about very large positions and it would affect very few entities," Assistant Treasury Secretary Darcy Bradbury said, adding "I would hope that we would use this regulation extremely rarely."
